## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Visālakkhivimānavatthu* ("Mansion of the Beautiful-Eyed Goddess", Vv 37) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. The work illustrates how keeping the moral precepts, living a restrained life, practicing generosity, and maintaining faith yield celestial happiness and high rebirth. In his commentary on the *Visālakkhivimāna* story (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* 169–172), Dhammapāla examines the distinction between performing a virtuous deed and its eventual "ripening" (*vipāka*) in a later existence, focusing on the verse declaration that one's former virtue had not yet ripened (*yañ ca sīlavatī āsiṁ na taṁ tāva vipaccati*) [Monius 2001].
